verdict.rationale: Viam documents official SDKs across Python, Go, C++, TypeScript (plus Flutter). Its APIs span machine control, fleet management and ML training, and the SDKs handle transport, sessions and reconnection. However, the docs assign the languages different roles (Python/Go for control logic, C++ for lower-level control, TypeScript for client apps), which suggests uneven coverage rather than full-surface parity. Missing for 10: evidence that the SDKs are typed, evidence that every language covers the full platform surface (fleet, data, ML, machine APIs), and independent or hands-on corroboration of SDK quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build against official, typed SDKs in multiple languages (Python, TypeScript, Go, C++) that cover the platform's full surface

citations.quote: Write your control logic in Python or Go, get lower-level control with C++, or build a client application with Typescript or Flutter.
Multiple SDKs are available for writing client applications that interface with the Viam RDK.
The machine API allows you to connect to your machine from within a supported Viam SDK, retrieve status information, and send commands remotely.
The fleet management API allows you to manage your machine fleet with code the same way you can do in the web UI.
They open the transport (WebRTC where appropriate, gRPC otherwise), manage sessions for safety, and reconnect automatically when the network drops.
